View original ARBA rule on UniProt

Type: ARBA
Status: COMPLETE
Action: ACCEPT
Confidence: 0.70
Rule as retrieved: 2026-11-15
Condition sets examined: 1010 of 1010

Description

Assigns the UniProt keyword Protease (KW-0645) through 1010 alternative condition sets. About half are single InterPro entries or PANTHER families; the rest are conjunctions of two or three conditions, some with a taxon.

The domain overlap table is not shown for this review. It is drawn from a cached analysis of the rule's condition sets, and the cache does not match the sets recorded here.

Review Summary

Accuracy: the first 10 of the 1010 live condition sets were examined. They select ClpP, HslV, leucyl aminopeptidase, peptidase M48 and signal peptidase II families, and every reviewed match carries the Protease keyword KW-0645 (5150 of 5150, summed over sets). All 1,010 sets were then scanned against Swiss-Prot (UniProtKB 2026_04, 2026-11-15): every set has reviewed matches, and 24,550 of the 24,551 set-level matches carry the keyword (5,150 in the first ten sets, 19,401 in the other 1,000). The exception is Q7SQ98 (Gag-Pol polyprotein of avian leukosis virus, set 888), whose record lists the cleavage product Protease p15 with EC 3.4.23.- but lacks the keyword; the sibling Gag polyprotein P0C776 carries Aspartyl protease. That is an omission in the entry, not a wrong match. Meaning and parsimony: the keyword names an enzyme class and the sampled sets select families of that class, so the rule is a coherent statement. Protease is the parent of eight class keywords (Aminopeptidase, Aspartyl protease, Carboxypeptidase, Dipeptidase, Metalloprotease, Serine protease, Thiol protease, Threonine protease), each with its own ARBA rule, and 605 of the 1,010 sets are word-for-word copies of a set in one of those eight rules (keyword_redundancy.tsv counts 612, because it also counts a set whose signatures contain those of a child-rule set). UniProt does not derive the parent keyword from a class keyword, so those shared sets are what puts Protease on the proteins they match; the overlap is not a defect.

Action Rationale

Every one of the 1,010 condition sets has reviewed matches and all but one of 24,551 carry the keyword; the one exception is a polyprotein that contains a protease and lacks the keyword. The keyword is meaningful at the level of a UniProt keyword and the sets select protease families. The overlap with the eight class-keyword rules is not a parsimony defect: UniProt does not derive Protease from a class keyword, so the shared sets are what puts Protease on those proteins. Confidence is not higher because the scan covers reviewed entries only.

Biological Meaning

COHERENT

Judged on the 10 recorded sets, which resolve into five protease families (see biological_units). The keyword is the class label that all of them share; class-specific keywords exist and are assigned by sibling rules. The keyword itself is the class label, so meaning is settled by the label and the family sample; the scan of all 1,010 sets is what supports accuracy. Overlap with child-keyword rules is in keyword_redundancy.tsv.

The consequent term has descendant terms. 612 condition set(s) are also matched by a rule asserting a more specific term. 10 condition set(s) were examined for this judgement.

Assessments

ACCEPTABLE

UniProt ARBA API, retrieved 2026-11-12: 605 of 1010 condition sets are identical (same conditions, same negation) to a set in one of the eight child-keyword rules. UniProt keywords API: KW-0645 is the parent of KW-0031, KW-0064, KW-0121, KW-0224, KW-0482, KW-0720, KW-0788 and KW-0888. UniProtKB search 2026-11-12: 0 entries carry any of those eight keywords without KW-0645. Within the sample, sets for one family also overlap: only 1 reviewed entry matches set 7 without matching set 5, and 42 match set 2 without matching set 1. No set's conditions are a superset of another set's. keyword_redundancy.tsv: 612 of 1,010 condition sets are also matched by a rule for a descendant keyword (Metalloprotease 199, Thiol protease 172, Serine protease 167, Aminopeptidase 47 and others; a set can be covered by more than one). Keywords from different rules stack on a protein, and UniProt does not derive a parent keyword from a child: in samples of 500 unreviewed entries each for Serine protease, Serine/threonine-protein kinase and Kinase (UniProtKB 2026_04, 2026-11-15) the parent keyword always carried its own rule evidence (ARBA, PROSITE-ProRule, HAMAP, PIRNR or RuleBase). So these sets do work: without them the proteins would lose this keyword.

APPROPRIATE

236 of 1010 sets carry a taxon. In the sample only set 10 does (Bacteria, for signal peptidase II), which is where that enzyme occurs.

Corrections (7)

Claims made by an earlier version of this review that were withdrawn, with the evidence that refuted them.

Withdrawn claimCorrection
The rule is a single condition set of 502 InterPro domains joined by OR, so any protein with any protease-related domain is annotated.
conjunction ignored · 2026-11-10		 The rule is a list of alternative condition sets, and the conditions inside a set are joined by AND. The live rule has 1010 sets; 497 require two or three conditions together.
  • UniProt ARBA API, ARBA00022670, modified 2026-07-18, retrieved 2026-11-09: 1010 condition sets (513 with one condition, 309 with two, 188 with three); every condition has a single value.
The rule has no taxonomic restrictions.
taxon misread · 2026-11-10		 236 of the 1010 live condition sets include a taxon condition.
  • UniProt ARBA API, ARBA00022670: 236 condition sets contain a condition of type taxon, for example set 10 (taxon Bacteria).
Treating pepsin, trypsin and other mechanistically distinct proteases the same is a design flaw, and the classification literature contradicts the rule.
general is not wrong · 2026-11-10		 All of these enzymes are proteases, which is all the keyword says. That proteases fall into mechanistic classes does not make the keyword wrong for any of them. The source given for the contradiction was an unattributed sentence labelled as a database, not a retrievable publication.
  • UniProtKB release 2026_04: in the ten sets examined every reviewed match carries keyword KW-0645; per-set counts are in the condition set notes.
Inactive zymogens and other non-catalytic proteins with protease domains would be annotated, giving massive false positives across 2.47 million proteins.
unexamined rule · 2026-11-10		 No falsely annotated protein was named and no rate was measured. Zymogens are protease precursors and carry the Protease keyword in Swiss-Prot.
  • The old file recorded no condition sets and no matched entries.
The rule is deficient because it assigns a keyword and not GO terms.
other · 2026-11-10		 The consequent is a UniProt keyword by design.
  • UniProt ARBA API, ARBA00022670: single annotation, keyword KW-0645 Protease.
No verdict is given because the rule was sampled and not examined set by set.
meaning not judged · 2026-11-12		 The sample is enough to judge meaning (the sets select protease families), and parsimony can be measured on the whole rule without reading every set: 605 of 1010 sets duplicate a set of a child-keyword rule, and the parent keyword follows automatically from the child. The rule should be reduced to the sets that have no class-specific counterpart.
  • UniProt ARBA API 2026-11-12: set-for-set comparison of ARBA00022670 with ARBA00022825, ARBA00023049, ARBA00022807, ARBA00022750, ARBA00022698, ARBA00022438, ARBA00022645 and ARBA00022997; 605 identical sets.
  • UniProtKB search 2026-11-12: keyword:KW-0720 NOT keyword:KW-0645 returns 0 entries; the same for KW-0482, KW-0788, KW-0064, KW-0888, KW-0031, KW-0121 and KW-0224.
Its construction is not economical: 605 of 1010 sets are copies of a set in a child-keyword rule, and because UniProtKB adds the parent keyword whenever a child keyword is present those sets cannot add an annotation; remove them (MODIFY, 0.6).
other · 2026-11-15		 That no entry carries a class keyword without Protease does not show the parent is added automatically: it is what one expects when a rule asserts each keyword. The evidence tags show the latter, so the shared sets are doing the work and removing them would remove the keyword.
  • UniProtKB 2026_04, 2026-11-15: of 500 unreviewed entries carrying KW-0720 (Serine protease), all carry KW-0645 (Protease) with evidence of its own, an ARBA or other rule in nearly every case; none carries it with a derived tag.
  • A0A8Q3WL70 carries Serine protease and Protease, each with an ARBA rule as its only evidence.

review_summary: >-
  Accuracy: the first 10 of the 1010 live condition sets were examined. They select ClpP, HslV, leucyl
  aminopeptidase, peptidase M48 and signal peptidase II families, and every reviewed match carries the
  Protease keyword KW-0645 (5150 of 5150, summed over sets). All 1,010 sets were then scanned against
  Swiss-Prot (UniProtKB 2026_04, 2026-11-15): every set has reviewed matches, and 24,550 of the 24,551
  set-level matches carry the keyword (5,150 in the first ten sets, 19,401 in the other 1,000). The exception
  is Q7SQ98 (Gag-Pol polyprotein of avian leukosis virus, set 888), whose record lists the cleavage product
  Protease p15 with EC 3.4.23.- but lacks the keyword; the sibling Gag polyprotein P0C776 carries Aspartyl
  protease. That is an omission in the entry, not a wrong match. Meaning and parsimony: the keyword names
  an enzyme class and the sampled sets select families of that class, so the rule is a coherent statement.
  Protease is the parent of eight class keywords (Aminopeptidase, Aspartyl protease, Carboxypeptidase,
  Dipeptidase, Metalloprotease, Serine protease, Thiol protease, Threonine protease), each with its own
  ARBA rule, and 605 of the 1,010 sets are word-for-word copies of a set in one of those eight rules (keyword_redundancy.tsv
  counts 612, because it also counts a set whose signatures contain those of a child-rule set). UniProt
  does not derive the parent keyword from a class keyword, so those shared sets are what puts Protease
  on the proteins they match; the overlap is not a defect.
action: ACCEPT
action_rationale: >-
  Every one of the 1,010 condition sets has reviewed matches and all but one of 24,551 carry the keyword;
  the one exception is a polyprotein that contains a protease and lacks the keyword. The keyword is meaningful
  at the level of a UniProt keyword and the sets select protease families. The overlap with the eight
  class-keyword rules is not a parsimony defect: UniProt does not derive Protease from a class keyword,
  so the shared sets are what puts Protease on those proteins. Confidence is not higher because the scan
  covers reviewed entries only.

parsimony:
  assessment: ACCEPTABLE
  notes: >-
    UniProt ARBA API, retrieved 2026-11-12: 605 of 1010 condition sets are identical (same conditions,
    same negation) to a set in one of the eight child-keyword rules. UniProt keywords API: KW-0645 is
    the parent of KW-0031, KW-0064, KW-0121, KW-0224, KW-0482, KW-0720, KW-0788 and KW-0888. UniProtKB
    search 2026-11-12: 0 entries carry any of those eight keywords without KW-0645. Within the sample,
    sets for one family also overlap: only 1 reviewed entry matches set 7 without matching set 5, and
    42 match set 2 without matching set 1. No set's conditions are a superset of another set's. keyword_redundancy.tsv:
    612 of 1,010 condition sets are also matched by a rule for a descendant keyword (Metalloprotease 199,
    Thiol protease 172, Serine protease 167, Aminopeptidase 47 and others; a set can be covered by more
    than one). Keywords from different rules stack on a protein, and UniProt does not derive a parent
    keyword from a child: in samples of 500 unreviewed entries each for Serine protease, Serine/threonine-protein
    kinase and Kinase (UniProtKB 2026_04, 2026-11-15) the parent keyword always carried its own rule evidence
    (ARBA, PROSITE-ProRule, HAMAP, PIRNR or RuleBase). So these sets do work: without them the proteins
    would lose this keyword.
